topic: Law change: stricter delayed birth & death registration from 1 Oct 2026 - over 2 years needs Judicial Magistrate order (Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026, Act 12 of 2026)

slides.kicker: Law change · In force from 1 Oct 2026
slides.title: Late birth registration is now **stricter**
slides.subtitle: If a birth or death was not registered on time, getting it on record late has become harder, especially after **two years**.
slides.cite: **Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026** (Act 12 of 2026) · amends Section 13(3) of the 1969 Act

slides.label: The new rule
slides.title: Two years is the **new line**
bullets: **1 to 2 years late:** you need an order from the **DM, SDM** or an Executive Magistrate authorised by the DM.
**More than 2 years late:** only a **Judicial Magistrate First Class** of the area where the event happened can order it.
In both cases, the facts are **verified** first and a prescribed fee must be paid.

slides.label: What changed
slides.title: Old cases now go to **court**
bullets: Earlier, an **executive magistrate's** order was enough even for very old cases.
Now, anything older than two years needs a **judicial** order, a higher level of scrutiny.
The government says the aim is to make people report births and deaths **on time**.

slides.label: Why it matters
slides.title: This certificate is **proof**
bullets: A birth or death certificate is accepted as **evidence** of the birth or death of a person.
Registration is **compulsory** under the Act, and the certificate gives a person legal identity.
Missing record in your family? If it is under two years late, act **now** before the court route applies.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: No need to **panic**
bullets: If you already have a certificate, you do **not** need to get a new one.
Very late registration is still possible. The route is now through the **Judicial Magistrate**.
Fee amounts are not stated in the reports. Check with your local registrar. This post is for information only, not legal advice.

lines: One important legal update every day, in simple words.

caption:
Is a birth or death in your family still not registered? Read this 📜⚖️

From 1 October 2026, the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 has made late registration stricter. If the event is reported more than one year but within two years late, you need an order from the DM, SDM or an Executive Magistrate authorised by the DM.

If it is more than two years late, only a Judicial Magistrate First Class of the area where the birth or death took place can order the registration. In both cases the facts are verified and a prescribed fee is charged. The government says the aim is to encourage timely reporting.

Why it matters: a birth or death certificate is accepted as evidence of that birth or death, and it gives a person legal identity. If you already have a certificate, you do not need a new one. If a record in your family is still missing, do not wait.

Law: Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 (Act 12 of 2026), amending Section 13(3) of the 1969 Act. In force from 1 Oct 2026.

This post is for information only, not legal advice.
